title: Best Snow Removal Software (2026): 6 Tools, Real Prices
description: Snow removal software compared: Plowdesk and Yardbook free plans, Yeti from $66.50/mo, Jobber, Housecall Pro, Service Autopilot. Per-push and per-inch billing.
h1: Best snow removal software for plow and snow contractors
body:
Snow removal software has one job that lawn and pool software doesn’t: when a storm hits, it has to dispatch every route at once, record proof of service (photos, timestamps, GPS) for slip-and-fall disputes, and turn the storm into correct invoices under each customer’s contract: per push, per event, per inch, hourly or a seasonal flat rate. Below are six tools whose snow features and prices we could verify on the vendors’ own pages on November 19, 2026: two snow-only apps (Plowdesk and Yeti) and four year-round field service tools that lawn and landscaping companies already use (Yardbook, Service Autopilot, Jobber, Housecall Pro). Anything a vendor doesn’t publish is marked unknown.

{{table:plowdesk,yeti-software,yardbook,service-autopilot,jobber,housecall-pro}}

Which snow billing models each tool documents

Start with how you bill, because that rules tools in or out fastest. This is what each vendor’s own pages or help center say, checked 2026-11-19:

What it costs: two example snow operations

Snow tools price by very different units: Yeti by sites, Plowdesk by storm-route limit (users are unlimited), Jobber and Housecall Pro by users per plan, Service Autopilot by plan with a set number of mobile licenses. Here is what each published price list gives for two typical setups (USD, before tax and card fees):

Solo plow operator, about 20 residential driveways

  • Plowdesk Operator: $0. Free with unlimited users and customers, up to 3 storm routes.
  • Yardbook Starter: $0. Includes the snow removal module (property-based pricing, snow route templates, Quick Dispatch). Online card payments on free accounts carry a 1% Yardbook fee on top of Stripe’s fees.
  • Yeti (1–25 sites): $95/mo billed monthly, or $66.50/mo billed annually ($798/yr).
  • Jobber Core: $49/mo with no commitment or $29/mo billed annually, but route optimization starts on Connect ($139/mo, or $99/mo billed annually).
  • Housecall Pro Basic: $79/mo or $59/mo billed annually. Routes start on Essentials ($189/mo, or $149/mo annually).
  • Service Autopilot: Snow Dispatch isn’t on Startup ($49/mo). It starts on Pro at $199/mo (annual subscription rate) plus a sign-up fee whose amount isn’t published.

Owner plus 3 drivers, about 40 sites

  • Plowdesk Contractor: $95/mo for unlimited users and unlimited storm routes, but Plowdesk says unlimited routes apply to residential service and commercial terms may differ. If 3 routes are enough, Operator stays free.
  • Yeti (26–50 sites): $245/mo monthly, or $171.50/mo billed annually ($2,058/yr). Users are unlimited, so adding drivers doesn’t change the price. Note the jump at site 26: the 1–25 band is $95/mo.
  • Jobber Connect, 5 users: $149/mo billed annually (route optimization and GPS tracking included on Connect).
  • Housecall Pro Essentials, 5 users included: $189/mo or $149/mo billed annually; route optimization and Recurring Service Plans are on MAX ($329/mo, or $299/mo annually, 8 users).
  • Service Autopilot Pro: $199/mo (annual rate) includes 1 business user and 2 mobile licenses, so a third driver means extra licenses at a price that isn’t published.
  • Yardbook: the pricing page doesn’t publish user limits. GPS tracking needs Business ($34.99/mo).

For other trades and team sizes, see the field service software pricing tracker and cost for 1 vs 5 users.

1. Plowdesk: free snow-only plan, unlimited users

Plowdesk is built only for snow contractors. The free Operator plan is an ongoing plan, not a trial, with no credit card: unlimited users and customers, up to three storm routes, site photos and service logging, quotes and invoices, manual customer notifications and Venmo payment tracking. Contractor ($95/mo) adds unlimited storm routes for residential customers, automated customer notifications, task scheduling, weather and property-data integrations, commercial-service tools and payment integrations; Plowdesk says discounts are available for prepaid subscriptions but doesn’t list the amount. Its FAQ (reviewed October 31, 2026) says quotes can cover seasonal, per-push, tiered per-inch, hourly and material charges; multiple drivers can work one shared route; and the iPhone/iPad and Android apps store data offline and sync when signal returns. Two limits to know: QuickBooks Online is a manual CSV export (no payment sync, no QuickBooks Desktop), and the customer portal is still being tested this season. {{aff:plowdesk|See Plowdesk plans}}

2. Yeti Software: snow-only, priced by sites

Yeti sells one plan, High Performance, priced by how many sites you manage, with unlimited users and clients at every band. From its pricing calculator: 1–25 sites $95/mo, 26–50 $245/mo, 51–100 $395/mo, 101–200 $495/mo, 201–300 $645/mo, 301–400 $795/mo and 401–500 $945/mo billed monthly; annual billing takes 30% off (for example $66.50/mo, or $798/yr, for 1–25 sites). There’s no free plan or trial listed; instead there’s a 60-day money-back guarantee. The platform page lists reusable multi-crew snow plow routes, a live dispatch hub, GPS crew tracking with geofencing and required photos, subcontractor management, SLA tracking, digital site inspections for slip-and-fall records, automatic client arrival/completion notifications, batch invoicing across sites and QuickBooks Online invoice generation. The crew app is in English, French and Spanish. Weather reporting is an add-on with no published price. {{aff:yetisoftware|See Yeti pricing}}

3. Yardbook: snow module on a free plan

Yardbook’s free Starter plan includes its snow removal module. Its tutorial walks through the workflow: set a property-based price for a “Snow Plowing” service (or separate services per depth band), build reusable snow route templates, use Quick Dispatch to create a job for every property on a route at once with a crew and date, then run the Auto Generate Invoice process using those prices. Business ($34.99/mo) adds GPS tracking, bulk email and text, automatic invoice reminders and waives the 1% Yardbook payment fee; Enterprise ($49.99/mo) adds QuickBooks sync and removes ads. Yardbook doesn’t document per-event or per-inch billing rules or seasonal snow contracts. More: Yardbook pricing and Yardbook vs Jobber. {{aff:yardbook|See Yardbook plans}}

4. Service Autopilot: the deepest snow billing rules

Service Autopilot documents the most detailed snow billing of the year-round tools. Its snow page lists pre-built master routes, adding or cancelling jobs from the app mid-storm, before-and-after photos with timestamps, two-way QuickBooks sync and billing per push, per event, per inch, hourly or flat rate. Its help center adds a Snow Dispatch Board organized by weather event (plan depth, bill depth, temperature, equipment) and seasonal contracts with caps by inches, pushes or events plus overage invoices. The catch is price and plan: Snow Dispatch starts on Pro ($199/mo), all published prices are annual subscription rates plus a sign-up fee whose amount isn’t listed, and QuickBooks Online sync is call-for-pricing below Elite. Its help center also notes that snow jobs are currently supported only in the legacy mobile app. See Service Autopilot pricing. {{aff:serviceautopilot|See Service Autopilot plans}}

5. Jobber: per-push billing with a workaround for depth

Jobber’s snow page lists quote add-ons (de-icing, monthly packages), a drag-and-drop schedule, map routing and route optimization, and team push notifications. Its help center describes the snow workflow: create one season-long recurring job per client set to “as needed”, then use the New Visits tool to add visits for many clients at once when it snows. Choose per-visit invoicing for per-push billing or fixed-price invoicing for seasonal contracts. Jobber doesn’t have per-inch rate tables; its help article says to make one job per depth band (for example under 6 inches and over 6 inches). Core is $29/mo billed annually ($49/mo with no commitment) for 1 user, but route optimization and GPS tracking start on Connect ($99/mo billed annually). Details: Jobber pricing. {{aff:jobber|See Jobber plans}}

6. Housecall Pro: seasonal contracts and fleet GPS

Housecall Pro’s snow page lists seasonal contracts, per-visit pricing and monthly snow plans, automated invoicing with auto-charge of cards on file, snow plow fleet GPS tracking with driving scores and dashcam footage, and iOS and Android apps in English and Spanish. On its pricing page, Routes and phone-based Employee GPS tracking start on Essentials ($149/mo billed annually, $189/mo monthly, 5 users), while route optimization and Recurring Service Plans are on MAX ($299/mo annually, $329/mo monthly, 8 users, $35/mo per extra user). The vehicle GPS (fleet tracking) price isn’t listed on either page. The snow page doesn’t describe per-inch or per-event billing. See Housecall Pro pricing. {{aff:housecallpro|See Housecall Pro plans}}

How to choose

  • Solo or residential-only, tight budget: start on Plowdesk Operator or Yardbook Starter, both $0. Plowdesk is snow-only with offline apps; Yardbook also runs your lawn season (see lawn care software).
  • Commercial lots, many sites, subcontractors: Yeti is built for that and doesn’t charge per user, but budget by site band.
  • Lawn and landscape company that adds snow in winter: Service Autopilot has the most complete snow billing rules; Jobber and Housecall Pro handle per-visit and seasonal billing if you don’t need per-inch rate tables.
  • Test a full storm before you commit: dispatch every route, log a second push at one property, and invoice the event, on the free plan or trial. Our software buying checklist has the questions to ask.

Other $0 options across trades: free field service software.

Landscapers adding snow to a crew operation: see landscaping business software for LMN, Aspire and Service Autopilot.
faq: What is the best snow removal software for a small business?

It depends on how you bill. For a solo or small residential operation, Plowdesk Operator and Yardbook Starter are both free (checked 2026-11-19). Plowdesk is snow-only, with up to 3 storm routes and unlimited users; Yardbook includes a snow module with route templates and Quick Dispatch. Service Autopilot documents the most snow billing options (per push, per event, per inch, hourly, flat rate), but Snow Dispatch starts on its Pro plan at $199/mo (annual rate) plus a sign-up fee.
Is there free snow removal software?

Yes. Plowdesk's Operator plan is free with no credit card: unlimited users and customers, up to three storm routes, site photos, quotes and invoices. Yardbook's free Starter plan includes its snow removal module, with a 1% Yardbook fee on online card payments (plus Stripe's fees) on free accounts.
How much does Yeti snow software cost?

Yeti prices by number of sites, with unlimited users and clients: $95/mo for 1-25 sites, $245/mo for 26-50 and $395/mo for 51-100 billed monthly, up to $945/mo for 401-500 sites. Annual billing is 30% less, e.g. $66.50/mo ($798/yr) for 1-25 sites. It has a 60-day money-back guarantee (yetisoftware.com/pricing, checked 2026-11-19).
Which snow removal software bills per push?

Service Autopilot has a 'Per Push, Per Inch' invoice type that bills each push from a rate matrix. Jobber's help center says to use per-visit invoicing for per-push billing. Plowdesk quotes can include per-push pricing, and Housecall Pro's snow page lists per-visit pricing.
Can I bill snow removal per inch?

Service Autopilot supports per-inch rates through a rate matrix by snow depth, and Plowdesk quotes can use tiered per-inch pricing. Jobber and Yardbook have no per-inch rate tables; both help guides suggest separate jobs or services for each depth band (for example under and over 6 inches).
Does snow removal software work with QuickBooks?

Yeti includes a QuickBooks Online integration. Service Autopilot lists two-way QuickBooks Online sync (included on Elite, call for pricing on Pro and Pro Plus). Jobber syncs with QuickBooks Online from Connect, Housecall Pro from Essentials, and Yardbook on Enterprise ($49.99/mo). Plowdesk uses a manual CSV export to QuickBooks Online, with no payment sync.
